records: Zen Internet was listed as an automatic-compensation scheme signatory.
Ofcom stated that automatic-compensation amounts increase annually in line with inflation.
Delayed-repair compensation applies when a stopped service is not fully fixed after two full working days.
The listed delayed-repair payment was £10.34 for each calendar day the service remained unrepaired.
A missed appointment includes an engineer failing to attend or cancellation with less than 24 hours' notice.
The listed payment for a missed appointment was £32.31.
The listed delayed-start payment was £6.46 for each calendar day of delay.
The automatic-compensation scheme covers residential fixed-broadband and landline products.
Ofcom published the Connected Nations Spring 2026 update on 13 May 2026.
The Spring 2026 update describes mobile and fixed-broadband availability as of January 2026.
The Spring 2026 publication is an interim update to Connected Nations 2025, whose data snapshot was July 2025.
Fixed-broadband availability reporting includes fixed-line and fixed-wireless-access networks.
The Spring 2026 update also reports take-up of full-fibre services.
The report defines decent broadband as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
Mobile coverage is reported using signal-strength predictions supplied by the four mobile network operators.
The update reports 5G standalone coverage as rollout continues.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises in January 2026.
Full-fibre availability covered 82% of the UK's 30.5 million homes.
Full-fibre availability increased by 1.2 million homes over the six months to January 2026.
Full-fibre take-up across residential and commercial premises reached 12.4 million connections.
Full-fibre take-up corresponded to 47% of all premises with full-fibre access.
Gigabit-capable broadband availability reached 89% of UK homes.
Gigabit-capable broadband was available to 27.1 million UK homes.
The July 2025 gigabit-capable availability comparison was 87%.
The July 2025 gigabit-capable availability comparison was 26.4 million homes.
Ofcom estimated that 4,000 premises lacked access to affordable decent broadband.
Ofcom estimated that 39,000 premises could not access decent broadband from fixed-line or fixed-wireless-access networks.
The comparable July 2025 count without decent fixed-line or fixed-wireless-access broadband was 44,000 premises.
